tasks.title: Recover signed admission after partial authoritative task assign
tasks.phase: Supervisor Runtime / Source-only Assistant Bridge Recovery
acceptance: Reproduce an ai_status assign that commits the exact signed task and provenance to the authoritative store, then exits nonzero while refreshing a derived view; the bridge currently emits a failed receipt with admission not attempted even though governed show returns the task.

Make dispatch and admission crash-consistent and idempotent: after a nonzero assign, perform authoritative task readback and continue only when the full task spec plus original signed provenance are exact; otherwise fail closed without an admission record.
Provide a governed recovery mechanism for the exact original failed packet id that does not require moving/editing pending, failed, receipt, replay, canonical state, or admission JSON by hand.

Keep replay collision, packet digest, task-spec hash, actor, source conversation/turn, document, owner/reviewer, and provenance mismatch checks fail closed; a new packet id must not overwrite provenance on an already-materialized task.

Add focused crash-point and concurrency tests for assign-before-derived-failure, exact authoritative readback, retry claim expiry, duplicate failed leaf, packet-id collision, conflicting task spec, conflicting provenance, and admission record durability.

Perform no live config edit, process signal, runtime promotion, manual canonical-state edit, worker dispatch bypass, supervisor scheduling change, or fleet-routing change; after merge, recovering the legacy-bootstrap packet is a separate governed operation.
tasks.summary: The original signed legacy-bootstrap packet committed its canonical task, then failed derived-view refresh before admission. Exact-id replay is pinned to failed/ and new-id replay correctly fails provenance. Repair only the assistant dev bridge transaction/recovery boundary so exact original provenance can be admitted after authoritative readback without hand-editing queue or state files.
